---

## 3. Authentication flow (THE KEY ONE) — end-to-end

### The `Authenticator` port and its output
- Port: `paigasus-iam-core/src/ports.rs:158-163`:
  ```rust
  #[async_trait] pub trait Authenticator: Send + Sync {
      async fn authenticate(&self, token: &str) -> Result<ValidatedClaims, AuthnError>;
  }
  ```
- Output `ValidatedClaims` (`paigasus-iam-core/src/authn.rs:54-64`): `issuer, subject, audiences, expires_at, email, name, locale, zoneinfo`.
- The OIDC impl: `OidcAuthenticator` in `src/adapters/oidc/validator.rs:41-46` / `authenticate` at `validator.rs:170-219` (length cap → header/alg/kid → unverified `iss` → issuer match → JWKS lookup → signature/claims → `ValidatedClaims`).

### The use-case that resolves a Principal from a token
- `AuthenticateToken<A,E,P,M,I,C>` in `src/application/authenticate_token.rs:61-92` (generic over `Authenticator` + repos + id/clock + `JitPolicy`).
- `resolve(token, Provisioning) -> Result<AuthnPrincipal, AuthnError>` (`authenticate_token.rs:99-139`): calls `self.authenticator.authenticate(token)`, looks up `find_by_issuer_subject`, JIT-provisions if `Enabled` + allowed, returns `AuthnPrincipal` (`principal_id, kind, status, issuer, subject, expires_at` — `authn.rs:68-76`).
- `introspect(token) -> PrincipalContext` (`authenticate_token.rs:144-164`): `resolve(.., Disabled)` (never provisions, D10) + pages memberships. `PrincipalContext` = principal + memberships + role_grants (`authn.rs:81-86`).
- `Provisioning::{Enabled,Disabled}` enum at `authenticate_token.rs:18-22`.

### The transport-agnostic `AuthContext` (the "attached principal")
- `src/adapters/auth.rs:18-22`:
  ```rust
  #[derive(Clone)] pub struct AuthContext {
      pub principal_id: PrincipalId, pub issuer: Issuer, pub subject: String,
  }
  ```
- `bearer_from_headers(&HeaderMap) -> Option<String>` (`auth.rs:28-39`) — the ONLY credential extractor, shared by both transports, ASCII-case-insensitive `Bearer`. **This is the single choke point: API-key bearer auth will need to decide, from the token string, whether it's an OIDC JWT or an API key.**

### HTTP enforcement middleware
- `src/adapters/http/auth_middleware.rs:29-59` `require_bearer(State(state), request, next)`:
  1. `bearer_from_headers(request.headers())` → 401 `AuthnApiError(InvalidToken(Malformed))` if absent (`auth_middleware.rs:31-42`), with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` only when header fully absent.
  2. `state.authn.resolve(&token, Provisioning::Enabled)` (`auth_middleware.rs:44`).
  3. On success: `state.bootstrap_seeder.ensure_platform_admin(...)` then `request.extensions_mut().insert(AuthContext {...})` and `next.run(request)` (`auth_middleware.rs:45-56`).
  4. On error: `AuthnApiError(err).into_response()`.

### gRPC enforcement layer
- `src/adapters/grpc/authn.rs` — a tower `Layer`/`Service` (interceptors are sync-only; `resolve` is async). `AuthLayer` (`authn.rs:61-78`), `AuthEnforce::call` (`authn.rs:110-143`): `is_exempt(path)` (`authn.rs:93-95` — health + `Introspect`), else `bearer_from_headers` → `state.authn.resolve(&token, Enabled)` → `ensure_platform_admin` → `req.extensions_mut().insert(AuthContext {...})` → `inner.call(req)`; rejects render via `convert::authn_status(err).into_http()` (`authn.rs:149-151`).
- gRPC `Introspect` handler: `AuthnGrpc` (`authn.rs:34-56`) calls `self.state.authn.introspect(&token)`.

### HTTP `AuthnError` funnel (distinct from tenancy `ApiError`)
- `src/adapters/http/authn.rs`: `AuthnApiError(pub AuthnError)` + `impl IntoResponse` (`authn.rs:29-59`) — 401 `invalid_token` (+`WWW-Authenticate`), 403 subcodes `identity_not_provisioned`/`provisioning_failed`/`principal_inactive`, 503 `unavailable`, 500 `internal`. The introspect route + body-limit is `authn::router(body_limit)` (`authn.rs:96-98`), handler `introspect` (`authn.rs:106-109`).
- `AuthnError` enum: `paigasus-iam-core/src/authn.rs:125-139` (`InvalidToken(TokenDefect)`, `IdentityNotProvisioned`, `ProvisioningFailed`, `PrincipalInactive`, `Unavailable`, `Backend`). `TokenDefect` at `authn.rs:103-114`.

### **Where API-key bearer auth plugs in as a SIBLING authenticator**
The cleanest mirror of the existing `WiredAuthenticator` enum dispatch (`mod.rs:78-92`):
- Option A (recommended, minimal blast radius): introduce a new **credential-router** step between `bearer_from_headers` and `resolve`. Both `require_bearer` (`auth_middleware.rs:44`) and `AuthEnforce::call` (`authn.rs:126`) currently call `state.authn.resolve(&token, Enabled)`. Add an API-key detector (e.g. key-prefix check on `token`) that, when matched, calls a NEW `state.api_key_auth.resolve(&token)` returning the SAME `AuthnPrincipal` (so the rest — `ensure_platform_admin`, `AuthContext` insertion — is unchanged). Both transports get the branch identically (they already duplicate the resolve call).
- Option B: implement a new use-case `AuthenticateApiKey` mirroring `AuthenticateToken`, producing an `AuthnPrincipal`. Note the domain currently models only `PrincipalKind::User` (`paigasus-iam-core/src/principal.rs:9-12` — comment says "`ServiceAccount` arrives in a later milestone"); API keys authenticating a service-account principal will need a new `PrincipalKind::ServiceAccount` variant there.
- Either way the token → `AuthContext` seam is centralized in `src/adapters/auth.rs` + the two enforcement call-sites; nothing downstream (handlers, authz) changes because they only read `AuthContext`/`AuthnPrincipal`.

---

## 4. OIDC/caching (reuse for hot-path API-key introspection)

**Cache trait abstraction + in-memory fallback** — `src/adapters/oidc/jwks.rs`
- `#[async_trait] pub trait JwksCache { get(&self, issuer) -> Result<Option<CachedJwks>>; put(...); }` (`jwks.rs:33-37`).
- In-memory fallback `InMemoryJwksCache(RwLock<HashMap<..>>)` — "Never fails … fallback used even when no external cache is configured" (`jwks.rs:39-61`).
- TTL/freshness + single-flight + cooldown orchestration in `JwksProvider` (`jwks.rs:173-262`), `is_fresh` (`jwks.rs:254-256`).

**Redis adapter (fail-CLOSED for auth)** — `src/adapters/oidc/redis_cache.rs`
- `RedisJwksCache { conn: ConnectionManager, ttl_secs }`, `connect(redis_url, ttl_secs)` (`redis_cache.rs:30-45`), key prefix `iam:jwks:<issuer>` (`redis_cache.rs:20-24`), TTL via `conn.set_ex(&key, payload, self.ttl_secs)` (`redis_cache.rs:63`). Every redis/serde error → `AuthnError::Unavailable` (fail closed, `redis_cache.rs:71-84`).

**Decision cache (fail-OPEN accelerator)** — `src/adapters/authz/decision_cache.rs`
- `#[async_trait] DecisionCache { get(key)->Option<Decision>; put(key,&Decision) }` port at `paigasus-iam-core/src/authz/ports.rs:58-62`.
- `MemoryDecisionCache(Mutex<HashMap<String,Decision>>)` (`decision_cache.rs:54-75`) + `RedisDecisionCache` with `from_connection(conn, ttl_secs)` sharing a connection (`decision_cache.rs:89-149`). **Fails OPEN**: get errors → `None`, put errors → logged+swallowed (`decision_cache.rs:116-149`). Key = generation-folded blake3 digest, `decision_key` (`decision_cache.rs:41-48`).

**Which to mirror for API-key introspection caching:** the **`RedisDecisionCache` fail-OPEN + `from_connection(shared_conn, ttl)` pattern** is the right model for a hot-path key lookup accelerator (a cache miss/outage must fall through to the DB, never fail the request). Use a `Memory*`/`Redis*` pair behind a trait, selected by the `AuthzCacheBackend`-style enum, and reuse the SAME shared `ConnectionManager` from `AppState::new` (see §6). Caution: an API-key introspection cache holds credential-authority material — decide fail-open (availability) vs fail-closed (like JWKS) deliberately.

---

## 5. Config — `src/config.rs`

- Loaded via **figment**: defaults `<` `iam.toml` `<` `IAM_*` env — `IamConfig::figment()` (`config.rs:217-219`), `load()` (`config.rs:224-226`), plus a hand-written `validate()` (`config.rs:242-321`).
- `IamConfig` (`config.rs:12-20`): `http_addr, grpc_addr, database_url, log_level, authn: AuthnConfig, authz: AuthzConfig`.
- `AuthnConfig` (`config.rs:25-42`): scalar `*_secs`, `max_token_bytes`, `accept_invalid_tls`, nested `jwks_cache: JwksCacheConfig`, `issuers: Vec<IssuerConfig>`.
- Cache backend modeling — the exact pattern to copy: `JwksCacheConfig { backend: JwksCacheBackend, redis_url: Option<String> }` + `enum JwksCacheBackend { Memory, Redis }` with `#[serde(rename_all="lowercase")]` (`config.rs:44-55`); mirrored by `AuthzCacheConfig`/`AuthzCacheBackend` (`config.rs:90-101`).
- Defaults pattern: a separate `#[derive(Serialize)] struct Defaults`/`AuthnDefaults`/`AuthzDefaults` (`config.rs:116-194`) fed into `Serialized::defaults`. `AuthzConfig` also gets a `Default` impl delegating to `AuthzDefaults` for hand-built test configs (`config.rs:200-213`).
- TTL fields already exist as `u64` seconds (e.g. `decision_cache_ttl_secs` `config.rs:84`), validated non-zero (`config.rs:284-293`).
- Feature-flag example: `enforce_tenancy: bool` (`config.rs:81`, default `true` `config.rs:182`).

**How to add API-key config:** add an `ApiKeyConfig` (hashing params like argon2/pbkdf2 cost, `key_prefix: String`, `introspect_cache_ttl_secs: u64`, and if cached a `cache: ApiKeyCacheConfig { backend, redis_url }`) as `pub api_keys: ApiKeyConfig` on `IamConfig` (`config.rs:12-20`); add matching `ApiKeyDefaults` to `Defaults` (`config.rs:116-148`) with a `Default` impl; and add validation (non-zero TTL, redis-url-when-redis, sane hashing params) to `validate()` following the `authz` block precedent (`config.rs:277-305`). Update `iam.toml.example` (crate root) which documents each block (`iam.toml.example:12-42`).

## ⚠️ Load-bearing correction to premise (2) up front

Your task says ServiceAccount "already exists as a Cedar entity type and needs to actually resolve as an entity." **That is not accurate for the Cedar *schema*.** The embedded schema declares only `Root, Organization, Team, Project, Principal` — there is no `ServiceAccount` (and no `User`) entity type. What you saw is two different things:

- `rs/crates/libs/paigasus-kernel/src/cedar.rs:52-54` — a unit test asserting the **pure PRN→string mapping** turns `service-account/<uuid>` into the string `"Pgs::Iam::ServiceAccount"`. This is just the injective pascal-case mapping; it does **not** put `ServiceAccount` in the Cedar schema.
- `.../migration/m0004_create_authz.rs:8-9` — an explicit comment: *"ServiceAccount was cut from M3 (GATE 1 decision) — this migration does not touch `PrincipalKind` or add a `service_account` table."*

The codebase instead uses a **single unified `Principal` Cedar entity type** for all principals, with a `kind` attribute (`"user"` today). This is the crux of your design decision — details below.

## Part A — Cedar authorization wiring

### A1. Cedar schema + write-time validation — `rs/crates/libs/paigasus-iam-core/src/authz/schema.rs`

The schema is one embedded human-syntax string, parsed once via `OnceLock` (`schema.rs:28-31`):

```
namespace Pgs::Iam {
  entity Root;
  entity Organization in [Root] { effective_status: String };
  entity Team in [Organization] { effective_status: String };
  entity Project in [Team] { effective_status: String };
  entity Principal { kind: String, status: String };      // <-- the ONE principal type

  action GetOrganization, ... , GrantRole, RevokeRole, ListRoleGrants
    appliesTo { principal: [Principal], resource: [Root, Organization, Team, Project] };
}
```
- **No `User`, no `ServiceAccount` entity type.** All 27 actions apply to `principal: [Principal]` only (`schema.rs:19-24`).
- `Principal` has attributes `kind: String, status: String` — this is where a `"service_account"` kind would live with **zero schema change**.
- Write-time validation: `validate_policy()` (`schema.rs:34-43`) parses the policy as a `PolicySet` and runs `cedar_policy::Validator::new(schema()).validate(&pset, ValidationMode::default())`; fails with `AuthzError::SchemaValidation`. Called on every policy `put`.
- Actions catalog is kept 1:1 with the schema in `authz/action.rs` (enum `Action`, `ALL`, `as_wire()`, `is_write()`, `is_restore()`, `cedar_uid()` → `Pgs::Iam::Action::"<wire>"`).

**Implication for ServiceAccount:** if SAs use the unified `Pgs::Iam::Principal` type (recommended), the schema, action catalog, and templates need **no change** — `Principal` already covers them. If instead you add a distinct `entity ServiceAccount`, you must edit `SCHEMA_SRC` (new entity + add it to every action's `appliesTo principal: [...]`) and every role template's `permit(principal == ?principal, ...)` still works since it's `== ?principal` (untyped slot), but the entity would have to be schema-declared or `Entities::from_entities(.., Some(schema()))` in the engine (see A3) rejects it.

### A2. Authz model — `authz/model.rs`, `authz/roles.rs`, `authz/action.rs`

- `RoleGrant` (`model.rs:143-150`):
```rust
pub struct RoleGrant {
    pub id: Uuid,
    pub principal: PrincipalId,   // wraps a Prn
    pub role_key: String,
    pub scope: GrantScope,        // Root | Node(TenancyNodeRef)
    pub linked_policy_id: String, // "grant:<uuid>"
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}
```
- `PrincipalId` is `PrincipalId(Prn)` (`value.rs:51`) — a thin newtype over a PRN, kind-agnostic. `from_prn`, `uuid()`, `prn()`, `canonical()`.
- `Role` (`model.rs:131-138`): `key`, `template_id`, `scope_kinds: Vec<NodeKind>`, `description`, `system`. The 7 system roles live in `roles.rs::system_roles()` (`platform_admin`, `org_admin/member`, `team_admin/member`, `project_admin/member`), each with a Cedar template whose **`policy_id == role.key`** (load-bearing convention, `roles.rs:5-13`, `engine.rs:8-13`).
- Role templates are `permit(principal == ?principal, action in [...], resource in ?resource)` (`roles.rs:232-246`). The `?principal` slot is untyped, so **any** principal entity type binds — Users and SAs alike.
- How a principal "becomes" a Cedar principal entity: purely via its PRN → `to_cedar_uid` (see A4). A grant links a template into a concrete policy binding `?principal` = grantee PRN's uid, `?resource` = scope PRN's uid (`engine.rs:159-168 link_grant`).

### A3. Authorizer port + engine — `authz/ports.rs`, `authz/engine.rs`

- Port (`ports.rs:16-19`):
```rust
#[async_trait] pub trait Authorizer {
    async fn is_authorized(&self, req: &AccessRequest) -> Result<Decision, AuthzError>;
}
```
- `AccessRequest` (`model.rs:78-84`): `{ principal: Prn, action: Action, resource: Prn, context: RequestContext }` — **principal and resource are both plain `Prn`s**; no principal-kind knowledge here.
- Engine (`engine.rs`): `PolicyEngine::compile(policies, grants)` folds static policies + templates + per-grant links into a `PolicySet`. `PolicyEngine::decide(policies, slice, req)` builds Cedar entities from the slice via `Entities::from_entities(built, Some(schema()))` (`engine.rs:108`) — **this is schema-validated**, so any entity whose `entity_type` isn't in `SCHEMA_SRC` fails and becomes a fail-safe `Deny`. Principal/resource uids are built through `to_cedar_uid(&req.principal)` / `to_cedar_uid(&req.resource)` (`engine.rs:110-113`).
- Other ports: `PolicyStore`, `RoleGrantStore` (`grant`, `revoke`, `list_all`, `list_by_principal`, `find`), `EntitySliceLoader`, `DecisionCache`, `AuditSink`.

### A4. PRN → Cedar EntityUid mapping — `rs/crates/libs/paigasus-kernel/src/cedar.rs:18-23`

```rust
pub fn to_cedar_uid(prn: &Prn) -> CedarUid {
    CedarUid {
        entity_type: format!("Pgs::{}::{}", pascal(prn.service()), pascal(prn.resource_type())),
        entity_id: prn.resource_id().as_hyphenated().to_string(),
    }
}
```
So the **PRN resource_type decides the Cedar entity type.** Verified real principal PRN shape (all `resource_type = "principal"` → `Pgs::Iam::Principal`):
- `application/create_user.rs:125`: `Prn::build("iam", "", None, "principal", uuid)`
- `application/authenticate_token.rs:354`: `format!("prn:pgs:iam:::principal/{principal}")`

### A4b. Entity slice loader — `services/.../adapters/persistence/pg_entity_slice.rs`

- `load(resource, principal)` (`:151-169`): seeds synthetic `Root`, walks the resource's tenancy ancestor chain (`load_chain`, `:47-123`) each parented up to Root with `effective_status` attrs, then appends the principal entity.
- **The one hardcode to change** — `principal_entity()` (`:131-146`):
```rust

    ("kind".to_string(), ContextValue::Str("user".to_string())),   // <-- hardcoded "user"
    ("status".to_string(), ContextValue::Str(status)),

```
Status is already read kind-agnostically from the `principal` table by PK (`principal::Entity::find_by_id(principal_prn.resource_id())`, `:132-139`), falling back to `"active"`. So to make SAs "resolve as an entity like a User," this must read `kind` from the `principal` row instead of hardcoding `"user"` (and, if you keep the unified type, SAs must have `resource_type="principal"` PRNs so `uid_pair` yields `Pgs::Iam::Principal`).

The `principal` table already has a `kind` column (`m0001_create_principal_and_user.rs:15,43`; entity model `entities/principal.rs` has `pub kind: String`), and `user` is a 1:1 detail table FK'd to `principal.id`. A `service_account` detail table would parallel `user`.

The Redis decorator `adapters/authz/entity_cache.rs` (`SliceCache`) wraps the loader, keyed `iam:authz:slice:<entity_gen>:<resource-prn>:<principal-prn>` (`:48-50`) — folds in **both** PRNs, fail-open on Redis errors. Kind-agnostic; no change needed.

### A5. Decision/entity caches + generations — `adapters/authz/decision_cache.rs`, `generation.rs`, `cedar_authorizer.rs`

- `Generations` (`generation.rs`): two counters `policy_gen` / `entity_gen`, memory or Redis backend (`INCR`/`GET` on `iam:authz:policy_gen` / `iam:authz:entity_gen`).
- `decision_key(policy_gen, entity_gen, req)` (`decision_cache.rs:41-48`): `iam:authz:dec:<policy_gen>:<entity_gen>:<blake3 of (principal.canonical, action, resource.canonical, context)>`. Any of the 6 inputs changing mints a new key.
- **Invalidation on a role-grant change:** `PgRoleGrantStore::grant`/`revoke` bump **`policy_gen`** best-effort (`pg_role_grants.rs:44-48, 124-142`) — grants compile into the policy set, so they live under policy_gen, not entity_gen. A grant/revoke → `policy_gen++` → new decision-cache key space → old decisions unreachable. Because a **ServiceAccount's grants go through the very same `PgRoleGrantStore`** (the `role_grant.principal_id` FK is to `principal.id`, kind-agnostic — `m0004:115, 124-133`), SA grant changes invalidate automatically with **no new mechanism**.
- `CedarAuthorizer::is_authorized` (`cedar_authorizer.rs:139-198`) orchestrates: `reload_if_stale` → read snapshot → decision-cache lookup (key policy component = `compiled.r#gen`) → on miss, `slices.load` + `PolicyEngine::decide` → audit → cache put. `ResourceNotFound` slice errors become a fail-closed `Deny`; other errors propagate.

### Application-layer gate you must respect — `application/roles.rs`

`parse_principal_prn` (`roles.rs:39-45`) hard-requires `prn.service()=="iam" && prn.resource_type()=="principal"`, else `InvalidPrn`. `grant`, `revoke`, `list` all route through it (`:156-202`), plus an anti-escalation check (actor must itself be authorized for `GrantRole` at the scope) and `resolve_scope` defense-in-depth. **Consequence:** if ServiceAccounts use `principal/<uuid>` PRNs, grant/revoke/list work unchanged; if they use `service-account/<uuid>` PRNs, `roles.rs` rejects them until you loosen this check.

### Net change surface to make ServiceAccount a first-class principal reusing the User path (Option A, recommended)
- **No change:** `schema.rs`, `action.rs`, `engine.rs`, `roles.rs` templates, `role_grant` table, `decision_cache.rs`, `generation.rs`, `cedar_authorizer.rs`, `entity_cache.rs`, `ports.rs`.

# Exploration Report: ServiceAccount as a first-class authz principal + ServiceAccount/ApiKey proto surface

## ⚠️ Load-bearing correction to premise (2) up front

Your task says ServiceAccount "already exists as a Cedar entity type and needs to actually resolve as an entity." **That is not accurate for the Cedar *schema*.** The embedded schema declares only `Root, Organization, Team, Project, Principal` — there is no `ServiceAccount` (and no `User`) entity type. What you saw is two different things:

- `rs/crates/libs/paigasus-kernel/src/cedar.rs:52-54` — a unit test asserting the **pure PRN→string mapping** turns `service-account/<uuid>` into the string `"Pgs::Iam::ServiceAccount"`. This is just the injective pascal-case mapping; it does **not** put `ServiceAccount` in the Cedar schema.
- `.../migration/m0004_create_authz.rs:8-9` — an explicit comment: *"ServiceAccount was cut from M3 (GATE 1 decision) — this migration does not touch `PrincipalKind` or add a `service_account` table."*

The codebase instead uses a **single unified `Principal` Cedar entity type** for all principals, with a `kind` attribute (`"user"` today). This is the crux of your design decision — details below.

---

## Part A — Cedar authorization wiring

### A1. Cedar schema + write-time validation — `rs/crates/libs/paigasus-iam-core/src/authz/schema.rs`

The schema is one embedded human-syntax string, parsed once via `OnceLock` (`schema.rs:28-31`):

```
namespace Pgs::Iam {
  entity Root;
  entity Organization in [Root] { effective_status: String };
  entity Team in [Organization] { effective_status: String };
  entity Project in [Team] { effective_status: String };
  entity Principal { kind: String, status: String };      // <-- the ONE principal type

  action GetOrganization, ... , GrantRole, RevokeRole, ListRoleGrants
    appliesTo { principal: [Principal], resource: [Root, Organization, Team, Project] };
}
```
- **No `User`, no `ServiceAccount` entity type.** All 27 actions apply to `principal: [Principal]` only (`schema.rs:19-24`).
- `Principal` has attributes `kind: String, status: String` — this is where a `"service_account"` kind would live with **zero schema change**.
- Write-time validation: `validate_policy()` (`schema.rs:34-43`) parses the policy as a `PolicySet` and runs `cedar_policy::Validator::new(schema()).validate(&pset, ValidationMode::default())`; fails with `AuthzError::SchemaValidation`. Called on every policy `put`.
- Actions catalog is kept 1:1 with the schema in `authz/action.rs` (enum `Action`, `ALL`, `as_wire()`, `is_write()`, `is_restore()`, `cedar_uid()` → `Pgs::Iam::Action::"<wire>"`).

**Implication for ServiceAccount:** if SAs use the unified `Pgs::Iam::Principal` type (recommended), the schema, action catalog, and templates need **no change** — `Principal` already covers them. If instead you add a distinct `entity ServiceAccount`, you must edit `SCHEMA_SRC` (new entity + add it to every action's `appliesTo principal: [...]`) and every role template's `permit(principal == ?principal, ...)` still works since it's `== ?principal` (untyped slot), but the entity would have to be schema-declared or `Entities::from_entities(.., Some(schema()))` in the engine (see A3) rejects it.

### A2. Authz model — `authz/model.rs`, `authz/roles.rs`, `authz/action.rs`

- `RoleGrant` (`model.rs:143-150`):
```rust
pub struct RoleGrant {
    pub id: Uuid,
    pub principal: PrincipalId,   // wraps a Prn
    pub role_key: String,
    pub scope: GrantScope,        // Root | Node(TenancyNodeRef)
    pub linked_policy_id: String, // "grant:<uuid>"
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}
```
- `PrincipalId` is `PrincipalId(Prn)` (`value.rs:51`) — a thin newtype over a PRN, kind-agnostic. `from_prn`, `uuid()`, `prn()`, `canonical()`.
- `Role` (`model.rs:131-138`): `key`, `template_id`, `scope_kinds: Vec<NodeKind>`, `description`, `system`. The 7 system roles live in `roles.rs::system_roles()` (`platform_admin`, `org_admin/member`, `team_admin/member`, `project_admin/member`), each with a Cedar template whose **`policy_id == role.key`** (load-bearing convention, `roles.rs:5-13`, `engine.rs:8-13`).
- Role templates are `permit(principal == ?principal, action in [...], resource in ?resource)` (`roles.rs:232-246`). The `?principal` slot is untyped, so **any** principal entity type binds — Users and SAs alike.
- How a principal "becomes" a Cedar principal entity: purely via its PRN → `to_cedar_uid` (see A4). A grant links a template into a concrete policy binding `?principal` = grantee PRN's uid, `?resource` = scope PRN's uid (`engine.rs:159-168 link_grant`).

### A3. Authorizer port + engine — `authz/ports.rs`, `authz/engine.rs`

- Port (`ports.rs:16-19`):
```rust
#[async_trait] pub trait Authorizer {
    async fn is_authorized(&self, req: &AccessRequest) -> Result<Decision, AuthzError>;
}
```
- `AccessRequest` (`model.rs:78-84`): `{ principal: Prn, action: Action, resource: Prn, context: RequestContext }` — **principal and resource are both plain `Prn`s**; no principal-kind knowledge here.
- Engine (`engine.rs`): `PolicyEngine::compile(policies, grants)` folds static policies + templates + per-grant links into a `PolicySet`. `PolicyEngine::decide(policies, slice, req)` builds Cedar entities from the slice via `Entities::from_entities(built, Some(schema()))` (`engine.rs:108`) — **this is schema-validated**, so any entity whose `entity_type` isn't in `SCHEMA_SRC` fails and becomes a fail-safe `Deny`. Principal/resource uids are built through `to_cedar_uid(&req.principal)` / `to_cedar_uid(&req.resource)` (`engine.rs:110-113`).
- Other ports: `PolicyStore`, `RoleGrantStore` (`grant`, `revoke`, `list_all`, `list_by_principal`, `find`), `EntitySliceLoader`, `DecisionCache`, `AuditSink`.

### A4. PRN → Cedar EntityUid mapping — `rs/crates/libs/paigasus-kernel/src/cedar.rs:18-23`

```rust
pub fn to_cedar_uid(prn: &Prn) -> CedarUid {
    CedarUid {
        entity_type: format!("Pgs::{}::{}", pascal(prn.service()), pascal(prn.resource_type())),
        entity_id: prn.resource_id().as_hyphenated().to_string(),
    }
}
```
So the **PRN resource_type decides the Cedar entity type.** Verified real principal PRN shape (all `resource_type = "principal"` → `Pgs::Iam::Principal`):
- `application/create_user.rs:125`: `Prn::build("iam", "", None, "principal", uuid)`
- `application/authenticate_token.rs:354`: `format!("prn:pgs:iam:::principal/{principal}")`
- `pg_role_grants.rs:111`: reconstructs grantee PRN as `Prn::build("iam","",None,"principal", m.principal_id)`

### A4b. Entity slice loader — `services/.../adapters/persistence/pg_entity_slice.rs`

- `load(resource, principal)` (`:151-169`): seeds synthetic `Root`, walks the resource's tenancy ancestor chain (`load_chain`, `:47-123`) each parented up to Root with `effective_status` attrs, then appends the principal entity.
- **The one hardcode to change** — `principal_entity()` (`:131-146`):
```rust
attrs: BTreeMap::from([
    ("kind".to_string(), ContextValue::Str("user".to_string())),   // <-- hardcoded "user"
    ("status".to_string(), ContextValue::Str(status)),
]),
```
Status is already read kind-agnostically from the `principal` table by PK (`principal::Entity::find_by_id(principal_prn.resource_id())`, `:132-139`), falling back to `"active"`. The uid is `uid_pair(principal_prn)` = `to_cedar_uid`. So to make SAs "resolve as an entity like a User," this must read `kind` from the `principal` row instead of hardcoding `"user"` (and, if you keep the unified type, SAs must have `resource_type="principal"` PRNs so `uid_pair` yields `Pgs::Iam::Principal`).
- `entity_gen()` delegates to the shared `Generations` handle (`:171-173`).

The `principal` table already has a `kind` column (`m0001_create_principal_and_user.rs:15,43`; entity model `entities/principal.rs` has `pub kind: String`), and `user` is a 1:1 detail table FK'd to `principal.id`. A `service_account` detail table would parallel `user`.

The Redis decorator `adapters/authz/entity_cache.rs` (`SliceCache`) wraps the loader, keyed `iam:authz:slice:<entity_gen>:<resource-prn>:<principal-prn>` (`:48-50`) — folds in **both** PRNs, fail-open on Redis errors. Kind-agnostic; no change needed.

### A5. Decision/entity caches + generations — `adapters/authz/decision_cache.rs`, `generation.rs`, `cedar_authorizer.rs`

- `Generations` (`generation.rs`): two counters `policy_gen` / `entity_gen`, memory or Redis backend (`INCR`/`GET` on `iam:authz:policy_gen` / `iam:authz:entity_gen`).
- `decision_key(policy_gen, entity_gen, req)` (`decision_cache.rs:41-48`): `iam:authz:dec:<policy_gen>:<entity_gen>:<blake3 of (principal.canonical, action, resource.canonical, context)>`. Any of the 6 inputs changing mints a new key.
- **Invalidation on a role-grant change:** `PgRoleGrantStore::grant`/`revoke` bump **`policy_gen`** best-effort (`pg_role_grants.rs:44-48, 124-142`) — grants compile into the policy set, so they live under policy_gen, not entity_gen. A grant/revoke → `policy_gen++` → new decision-cache key space → old decisions unreachable. Because a **ServiceAccount's grants go through the very same `PgRoleGrantStore`** (the `role_grant.principal_id` FK is to `principal.id`, kind-agnostic — `m0004:115, 124-133`), SA grant changes invalidate automatically with **no new mechanism**.
- `CedarAuthorizer::is_authorized` (`cedar_authorizer.rs:139-198`) orchestrates: `reload_if_stale` → read snapshot → decision-cache lookup (key policy component = `compiled.r#gen`) → on miss, `slices.load` + `PolicyEngine::decide` → audit → cache put. `ResourceNotFound` slice errors become a fail-closed `Deny`; other errors propagate.

### Application-layer gate you must respect — `application/roles.rs`

`parse_principal_prn` (`roles.rs:39-45`) hard-requires `prn.service()=="iam" && prn.resource_type()=="principal"`, else `InvalidPrn`. `grant`, `revoke`, `list` all route through it (`:156-202`), plus an anti-escalation check (actor must itself be authorized for `GrantRole` at the scope) and `resolve_scope` defense-in-depth. **Consequence:** if ServiceAccounts use `principal/<uuid>` PRNs, grant/revoke/list work unchanged; if they use `service-account/<uuid>` PRNs, `roles.rs` rejects them until you loosen this check.

### Net change surface to make ServiceAccount a first-class principal reusing the User path (Option A, recommended)
- **No change:** `schema.rs`, `action.rs`, `engine.rs`, `roles.rs` templates, `role_grant` table, `decision_cache.rs`, `generation.rs`, `cedar_authorizer.rs`, `entity_cache.rs`, `ports.rs`.
- **Change:** `pg_entity_slice.rs:144` (read `kind` from the principal row, not hardcoded `"user"`); `principal.rs` `PrincipalKind` enum (`:9-12`, add `ServiceAccount` + `as_str`/`parse` arms); new `service_account` detail table + migration (parallel to `user`, m0001); mint SAs as `principal` rows with `kind="service_account"` and a `principal/<uuid>` PRN.
- **Alternative (Option B, distinct `Pgs::Iam::ServiceAccount` type):** edit `SCHEMA_SRC` (+`appliesTo`), give SAs `service-account/<uuid>` PRNs, and loosen `roles.rs::parse_principal_prn`. More invasive; diverges from the unified-`Principal` design and your own "authorized exactly like a User" requirement. The kernel `cedar.rs` mapping test hints this was once contemplated, but the schema/migrations deliberately did not go this way.

---

## Part B — Proto contracts (`contracts/proto/paigasus/iam/v1/iam.proto`)

### B6. Package, services, messages, conventions

- **Package:** `paigasus.iam.v1` (`iam.proto:4`); imports `google/protobuf/timestamp.proto` and `paigasus/common/v1/audit.proto`.
- **Three services:**
  - `TenancyService` (`:239-263`) — org/team/project CRUD + memberships (M1).
  - `AuthnService` (`:265-267`) — just `Introspect` (M2). D4 note: AuthorizationService's planned Introspect folded here.
  - `AuthorizationService` (`:331-339`) — `IsAuthorized`, `PutPolicy`, `DeletePolicy`, `ListPolicies`, `GrantRole`, `RevokeRole`, `ListRoleGrants` (M3).
- **Conventions:**
  - **PRNs as `string` fields** named `prn` / `<thing>_prn` (`principal_prn`, `node_prn`, `scope_prn`, `org_prn`, `team_prn`). No dedicated PRN type.
  - **Timestamps:** `google.protobuf.Timestamp` (e.g. `IntrospectResponse.expires_at`, `:228`). Entity audit fields via embedded `paigasus.common.v1.AuditMetadata audit = N;` (`Organization.audit`, etc.; `audit.proto` = created_at/modified_at/created_by/modified_by).
  - **Status enums:** `enum NodeStatus { NODE_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED=0; NODE_STATUS_ACTIVE=1; NODE_STATUS_ARCHIVED=2; }` (`:24-28`) — `UPPER_SNAKE`, zero = `_UNSPECIFIED`, prefixed with the enum name.
  - **Pagination:** request carries `uint32 limit` + `uint64 offset` (`limit 0 => server default 50`, `:78-81`); response has a single `repeated` field. See `ListOrganizations*`, `ListRoleGrants*` (`:322-329`).
  - **RPC message pairing:** every RPC has `XxxRequest`/`XxxResponse`; empty responses are `message DetachMembershipResponse {}` (`:207`).
  - **Field naming:** `lower_snake_case`; `oneof filter { ... }` for either/or filters (`ListMembershipsRequest`, `:208-215`); `optional` for nullable update fields (`RenameOrganizationRequest.new_slug`, `:87`).
  - **Enums-as-strings on the wire in some places:** `IsAuthorizedRequest.action` and `RoleGrant.scope_prn`/`role_key` are plain strings; `IntrospectResponse.status` is a `string` "principal status." `reserved`+add is used for evolution (`IntrospectResponse` `reserved 7; reserved "role_group_prns";`, `:230-232`).
- **Representative messages:** `RoleGrant { id, principal_prn, role_key, scope_prn }` (`:304-309`), `GrantRoleRequest { principal_prn, role_key, scope_prn }` (`:310-314`), `Policy { policy_id, kind, source, description, system }` (`:280-286`), `Membership { id, principal_prn, node_prn, audit }` (`:57-62`).

### B7. Where ServiceAccount + ApiKey fit
- **New messages** `ServiceAccount`/`ApiKey` fit alongside `Organization`/`Membership` as top-level messages carrying `string prn`, name/status fields, and an embedded `AuditMetadata audit`.
- **RPCs:** two natural options —
  1. A **new `ServiceAccountService`** (Create/Get/List/Rename/Archive/Restore ServiceAccount; CreateApiKey/RevokeApiKey/ListApiKeys) mirroring `TenancyService`'s CRUD shape. Register it in the tonic router exactly like the others (`adapters/grpc/mod.rs:54-56`, `add_service(...Server::new(...))`).
  2. Or fold onto existing services if you consider SAs a tenancy/identity concern.
  - Because grants are principal-kind-agnostic, **no new grant RPCs are needed** — existing `GrantRole/RevokeRole/ListRoleGrants` already accept any `principal_prn`.
- **Key wire decision mirrors the A1/roles.rs decision:** if SAs are unified `principal/<uuid>` PRNs, they slot straight into `GrantRoleRequest.principal_prn` and `AttachMembershipRequest.principal_prn` with no server-side parse changes; if they get `service-account/<uuid>` PRNs, the server `parse_principal_prn` must be loosened.

### Buf / Rust codegen setup
- `contracts/buf.gen.yaml`: `version: v2`, `clean: true`. Rust via **pinned remote plugins** `buf.build/community/neoeinstein-prost:v0.5.0` (opts `bytes=.`, `file_descriptor_set`) and `neoeinstein-tonic:v0.5.0` (opts `no_include`, `compile_well_known_types`), output → `rs/crates/libs/paigasus-proto/src/generated`. Also emits Python (betterproto2) and TS (protobuf-es).
- `contracts/buf.yaml`: lint `STANDARD` (except `PACKAGE_DIRECTORY_MATCH`); breaking `FILE` with `FIELD_NO_DELETE_UNLESS_NAME/NUMBER_RESERVED` so the reserve-and-add pattern is legal.
- Generated Rust is **committed** and re-exported via `include!` in `paigasus-proto/src/lib.rs:27-34` (`paigasus::iam::v1`), with `#![allow(clippy::all, warnings)]`. Regenerate with `moon run contracts:generate` (`paigasus-proto/moon.yml` deps on `contracts:generate`). Generated files: `generated/paigasus/iam/v1/paigasus.iam.v1.rs` (+ `.tonic.rs`). Server stubs consumed as `authorization_service_server::AuthorizationServiceServer`, etc. (`adapters/grpc/mod.rs:21-23`).

---

### One-line takeaways for your design
1. **ServiceAccount should reuse the unified `Pgs::Iam::Principal` entity** (PRN `prn:pgs:iam:::principal/<uuid>`, distinguished by the `kind` attr). That gets you "resolves as an entity, holds RoleGrants, authorized exactly like a User" with changes confined to `pg_entity_slice.rs` (the hardcoded `kind="user"`), the `PrincipalKind` enum, and a new `service_account` detail table — nothing in the Cedar schema, engine, grant store, or caches.
2. It is **not** currently a Cedar entity type; only the pure PRN→string mapping (kernel `cedar.rs`) knows the name `Pgs::Iam::ServiceAccount`. Adding a distinct type is possible but fights the existing unified-Principal design and the `roles.rs` `resource_type=="principal"` gate.
3. Cache invalidation for SA grant changes is already automatic via `policy_gen` bumps in `PgRoleGrantStore`.

content.text:
Here's what the exploration surfaced — including one important correction to my intake:

**Corrected picture: ServiceAccount is *not* yet a Cedar entity type.** M3 uses a single unified `Pgs::Iam::Principal` Cedar entity with a `kind` attribute (`"user"` today). The kernel has a PRN→string mapping that *knows the name* `Pgs::Iam::ServiceAccount`, but the schema, `role_grant` table, engine, and caches are all principal-kind-agnostic. m0004 explicitly records that "ServiceAccount was cut from M3 (GATE 1 decision)" — so **M4 is its intended home**.

**What that means for the change surface (the good news):** if a ServiceAccount is modeled as a `principal/<uuid>` PRN with `kind="service_account"`, then role grants, the grant store, decision/entity caches, and cache-invalidation-on-grant-change all work *automatically* — the only authz touch-point is un-hardcoding `kind="user"` in `pg_entity_slice.rs`. The domain follows the M1 `Principal`↔`User` template exactly: add `PrincipalKind::ServiceAccount`, a `service_account` detail table (parallel to `user`), and a two-row-in-one-txn insert.

**The genuinely new / undecided parts** are: key hashing, key wire format + constant-time validation, hot-path introspection caching vs revocation, key scope semantics, and how a non-OIDC (key-authenticated) principal flows through the auth middleware.

Before I draft the design, four load-bearing decisions I can't confidently default for you (I'll state my defaults for the smaller ones below). I'm batching them since they're orthogonal and you wrote the issue — tell me if you'd rather go one at a time.

questions.question: How should API keys be hashed at rest? (They're high-entropy random tokens, not human passwords — and they hit a validation hot path.)

options.label: HMAC-SHA-256 + pepper (Recommended)
options.description: Fast, constant-time, deterministic → enables an indexed lookup. A server-side pepper (config secret) means a DB leak alone can't validate keys. Correct for high-entropy tokens (GitHub/Stripe model). Recorded in the ADR.

options.label: Plain SHA-256
options.description: Same speed/lookup benefits, no secret to manage — but a DB dump alone lets an attacker verify guessed keys (moot at 256-bit entropy, but weaker defense-in-depth).

options.label: Argon2id
options.description: Memory-hard, slow by design. Meant for low-entropy passwords; overkill for random tokens and expensive on every cache miss. The issue lists it as an option but it fights the hot-path goal.

questions.question: What authorizes a request made with an API key?

options.label: Key authenticates as the SA; policy authorizes (Recommended)
options.description: The key proves 'I am ServiceAccount X'; authorization comes entirely from the SA's M3 role grants. The key stores scope PRN + optional action/role metadata, but v1 does NOT enforce key-level downscoping (stored for a later milestone). Matches the AC 'authorized by policy (M3)'.

options.label: Enforce key-level downscope in v1
options.description: Authorization = intersection of the SA's grants AND the key's action/role scope, injected into the Cedar request context. More plumbing; genuine attenuation now.

options.label: Key carries its own grant (capability)
options.description: The key embeds its own role/action scope and authorizes directly, independent of the SA's grants. Diverges from the SA-as-principal model.

questions.question: How should the ServiceAccount be modeled for Cedar authorization?

options.label: Unified Principal + kind attr (Recommended)
options.description: SA = principal/<uuid> PRN, kind='service_account'. Reuses the entire M3 path (grants, caches, invalidation) unchanged; only change is reading `kind` from the principal row instead of hardcoding 'user'. Matches 'authorized exactly like a User'.

options.label: Distinct Cedar ServiceAccount entity type
options.description: Add `entity ServiceAccount` to the schema, list it in every action's appliesTo, give SAs service-account/<uuid> PRNs, and loosen the roles.rs 'must be principal PRN' gate. More invasive; diverges from the unified design.

questions.question: Hot-path introspection is 'cached' (per the issue). How do we keep a revoked/expired key from being honored from cache?

options.label: Cache + per-key evict on revoke (Recommended)
options.description: Redis positive-validation cache (reusing M3's shared connection), short TTL, keyed by key-id; revoke/expire evicts the entry so denial is immediate. Expiry also enforced on read. Satisfies both 'hot-path cached' and 'revoked keys are denied'.

options.label: Short-TTL cache, accept bounded staleness
options.description: Cache with a short TTL and no explicit eviction; a revoked key may still be honored until the TTL lapses. Simpler, but weakens the 'revoked keys are denied' AC to 'denied within TTL'.

options.label: No cache in v1 (DB per request)
options.description: Validate against Postgres on every request; always correct, simplest, but not the 'hot-path cached' introspection the issue calls for. Add caching in a follow-up.

questions.question: How should the ServiceAccount be modeled for Cedar authorization?

options.label: Unified Principal + kind attr (Recommended)
options.description: SA = principal/<uuid> PRN, kind='service_account'. Reuses the entire M3 path (grants, caches, invalidation) unchanged; only change is reading `kind` from the principal row instead of hardcoding 'user'. Matches 'authorized exactly like a User'.

options.label: Distinct Cedar ServiceAccount entity type
options.description: Add `entity ServiceAccount` to the schema, list it in every action's appliesTo, give SAs service-account/<uuid> PRNs, and loosen the roles.rs 'must be principal PRN' gate. More invasive; diverges from the unified design.

questions.question: Hot-path introspection is 'cached' (per the issue). How do we keep a revoked/expired key from being honored from cache?

options.label: Cache + per-key evict on revoke (Recommended)
options.description: Redis positive-validation cache (reusing M3's shared connection), short TTL, keyed by key-id; revoke/expire evicts the entry so denial is immediate. Expiry also enforced on read. Satisfies both 'hot-path cached' and 'revoked keys are denied'.

options.label: Short-TTL cache, accept bounded staleness
options.description: Cache with a short TTL and no explicit eviction; a revoked key may still be honored until the TTL lapses. Simpler, but weakens the 'revoked keys are denied' AC to 'denied within TTL'.

options.label: No cache in v1 (DB per request)
options.description: Validate against Postgres on every request; always correct, simplest, but not the 'hot-path cached' introspection the issue calls for. Add caching in a follow-up.

answers.What authorizes a request made with an A: Key authenticates as the SA; policy authorizes (Recommended)

content.text:
## Stage 1 design — M4: Service accounts & API keys

Your four answers lock the architecture. Here's the full design; I've marked smaller calls as **[my default — say the word to change]**.

### Token format & constant-time validation (the crux of the AC)
Token shown once at creation:
```
pgs_sk_<keyid_b64url>_<secret_b64url>
```
- `keyid` = the ApiKey's UUIDv7 (kernel-minted) → embedded so introspection is an **O(1) primary-key lookup**, not a scan.
- `secret` = 32 random bytes (256-bit entropy) from the injected entropy source.
- **Stored:** `key_hash = HMAC-SHA-256(pepper, secret)`, plus a display `prefix` (`pgs_sk_<first-8-of-keyid>`) for list views, plus status/expiry/scope. The plaintext token is **never** persisted.
- **Validate:** parse & length-cap → b64url-decode `keyid` → PK lookup → `Hmac::<Sha256>::verify_slice(stored_hash)` (RustCrypto's HMAC verify is inherently **constant-time** — no separate `subtle` dep) → check `status = active` and `expires_at` unset-or-future. Malformed input → `ApiKeyDefect` (detail in `Debug` only, never in `Display`/logs — mirrors `TokenDefect`). New deps: `hmac` (+ existing `sha2`, `base64`, `rand`).

### 1. Domain (`paigasus-iam-core`)
- `principal.rs`: add `PrincipalKind::ServiceAccount` ("service_account") + `as_str`/`parse`/test. (No `principal.kind` CHECK exists, so no ALTER.)
- New `service_account.rs`: `ServiceAccount { principal_id, owner: TenancyNodeRef, name, status, created_at, updated_at }` — follows the `User` template (references `Principal` by id).
- New `api_key.rs`: `ApiKeyId(Uuid)`, `ApiKey { id, service_account_id, scope: TenancyNodeRef, prefix, status: ApiKeyStatus{Active,Revoked}, expires_at: Option, last_used_at: Option, created_at, revoked_at: Option, scope_actions/scope_roles: stored metadata }`, plus `ApiKeyDefect`/secret-scrubbing error.
- `authn.rs`: generalize the authenticated principal for non-OIDC credentials — replace the flat OIDC `issuer`/`subject` on `AuthnPrincipal` with a `Credential` enum (`Oidc { issuer, subject }` | `ApiKey { key_id }`). **[my default — smallest change that keeps API-key auth honest; downstream only reads `principal_id`]**
- `ports.rs`: `IdGenerator::new_service_account_id()` + `new_api_key_id()`; new `ServiceAccountRepository` + `ApiKeyRepository` (`#[async_trait]`, return `RepositoryError`); a `KeyHasher`/secret port so hashing is injectable & testable.

### 2. Persistence — migration `m0005_create_service_accounts_and_api_keys`
- `service_account` (shared PK `principal_id` FK→`principal` ON DELETE CASCADE, `owner_*` node columns + `ck_` scope check like `role_grant`, `name`, `status`, timestamps; `uq_service_account_owner_name`).
- `api_key` (UUID PK, FK→`service_account`, `key_hash` unique, `prefix`, `scope_*` node cols, `status`, `expires_at`, `last_used_at`, `created_at`, `revoked_at`; `ix_api_key_service_account`). Named constraints via raw SQL (load-bearing for `conflict_kind`), registered in `migration/mod.rs` + `entities/mod.rs`. New `ConflictKind` variants + `conflict_kind` branches.
- Creation mirrors `create_user`: **principal row + service_account row in one txn**. Issuing a key is a single insert.
- `last_used_at`: **throttled best-effort** — updated at most once per configurable interval (default 60s), off the request's critical path, errors swallowed. **[my default]**

### 3. Application services
- `CreateServiceAccount`, `create/list/archive` (mirror `CreateUser` + `RoleService`), `IssueApiKey`/`RevokeApiKey`/`ListApiKeys` — each `authorize.check(actor, Action::…, resource)` before mutating.
- `AuthenticateApiKey` use case (mirrors `AuthenticateToken`): validate token (cached) → return `AuthnPrincipal` for the SA. `introspect_api_key` returns `PrincipalContext` (principal + role grants).

### 4. Authn wiring (bearer API-key auth)
- One credential-router branch at the two existing seams (`http/auth_middleware.rs`, `grpc/authn.rs`): if the bearer string starts with `pgs_sk_` → `AuthenticateApiKey`, else the existing OIDC `resolve`. Both yield an `AuthnPrincipal` → identical `AuthContext` insertion. Nothing downstream changes.

### 5. Authz
- SA = unified `Pgs::Iam::Principal` (`principal/<uuid>` PRN, `kind="service_account"`). **Only authz change:** `pg_entity_slice.rs` reads `kind` from the principal row instead of hardcoding `"user"`. Grants, decision/entity caches, and grant-change invalidation all work unchanged (`role_grant.principal_id` is kind-agnostic).
- **New management actions** added to the Cedar schema `SCHEMA_SRC`, `action.rs` enum, and wired into system-role templates: `CreateServiceAccount`, `GetServiceAccount`, `ListServiceAccounts`, `ArchiveServiceAccount`, `IssueApiKey`, `RevokeApiKey`, `ListApiKeys` (granted to `platform_admin` + `org_admin`, scoped by the owner node). **[my default — fine-grained to match the existing 27-action convention; we could collapse to `ManageServiceAccounts`/`ManageApiKeys` if you prefer fewer]**

### 6. Introspection + caching
- Redis positive-validation cache reusing M3's shared `ConnectionManager`, keyed by `keyid`, short TTL; **revoke/expire evicts the entry** (immediate denial). Cache miss/outage falls through to Postgres. Memory + Redis impls behind a trait, selected by config (mirrors the authz cache backend enum).

### 7. Transport + proto (`contracts/proto/paigasus/iam/v1/iam.proto`)
- New `ServiceAccountService`: SA CRUD + `IssueApiKey`/`RevokeApiKey`/`ListApiKeys`. `IssueApiKeyResponse` carries the one-time plaintext token; `ListApiKeys` returns records **without** secrets (prefix + status + last_used + expiry).
- Key introspection endpoint mirroring token introspect: `POST /v1/authn/api-keys/introspect` + gRPC (unauthenticated, body-limited). Uses the cached path.
- Grants need **no new RPCs** — existing `GrantRole`/`RevokeRole` already accept any `principal_prn`.
- ApiKey addressed by UUID in the mgmt API (`/{id}`, mirrors role-grants). No separate PRN for the key. **[my default]**

### 8. Config + ADR
- New `ApiKeyConfig`: `pepper` (required secret via env/figment), `key_prefix`, `max_token_bytes`, `default_expiry`, `last_used_throttle_secs`, `introspect_cache: { backend, redis_url, ttl_secs }`. Validation in `validate()`; documented in `iam.toml.example`.
- Writes the **"API-key & secret handling" ADR** (Notion, per issue) recording: HMAC-SHA-256+pepper over argon2, token structure, shown-once, constant-time verify, cache-evict-on-revoke.

### 9. Testing
- **Domain unit** tests (kind round-trip, token parse/format, expiry/status logic).
- **Property-based** (`proptest`, new dev-dep) for key validation: round-trip issue→validate always succeeds; any bit-flip/truncation/wrong-pepper → reject; revoked/expired → reject; malformed never panics.
- **Integration** (testcontainers, mirroring `authz_*`/`tenancy_*`): issue→introspect→act (authorized by an SA role grant), revoke→denied, expiry→denied, cache-evict-on-revoke, HTTP + gRPC parity.

### Out of scope for v1 (explicit)
Key-level action/role **downscope enforcement** (metadata stored, not enforced — deferred); key rotation/auto-expiry sweeps; per-key rate limiting; distinct Cedar `ServiceAccount` entity type.

---

This is a sizable but well-bounded slice that follows the M1/M3 grain closely. **Does this design look right — and are the four `[my default]` calls (Credential enum, throttled last_used, fine-grained actions, UUID-addressed keys) fine as-is?** Once you approve, I'll write it up as the spec doc, then run the adversarial spec-challenger before the formal GATE 1 approval.

# SMA-445: M4 API keys & service accounts — Design

- **Issue:** [SMA-445](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-445) · Epic M4 of 6 · IAM v1 vertical slice
- **Date:** 2026-07-10
- **Status:** Draft (pre-GATE 1; Stage 2 adversarial challenge pending — see §18)
- **Governing ADRs:** the **API-key & secret handling ADR** (opened by this epic; number
  assigned in Notion), ADR-0013 (Cedar authorization — the policy path an SA is authorized
  through), ADR-0014 (tenancy hierarchy & PRN scheme — SA/key scope nodes), ADR-0015
  (Authenticator port — API-key auth is a sibling authenticator), ADR-0005 (kernel-first;
  PRN + `to_cedar_uid`), ADR-0004 (proto contracts), ADR-0006 (open-core boundary).
- **Precedents:** `2026-07-07-sma-444-m3-authorization-cedar-design.md` (M3 authz — reused
  wholesale), `2026-07-06-sma-443-m2-authentication-design.md` (M2 authn — sibling credential
  path), `2026-07-05-sma-442-m1-tenancy-design.md` (M1 tenancy — `Principal`↔`User` template),
  `2026-06-30-sma-448-kernel-prn-design.md` (PRN + `to_cedar_uid`).

## 1. Context & goal

M1 shipped the tenancy spine and the `Principal`↔`User` two-table pattern; M2 added OIDC-bearer
authentication; M3 added the embedded Cedar authorizer, roles-as-grants, and the decision/entity
caches. Every one of those was built kind-agnostic on a **single `Pgs::Iam::Principal` Cedar
type** whose `kind` attribute was deliberately left forward-compatible with `service_account`
(M3 spec D3/D5; `m0004` header records "ServiceAccount was cut from M3 (GATE 1 decision)").

M4 adds **machine identity**: a `ServiceAccount` principal owned by a tenancy node, and
issuable/revocable `ApiKey`s scoped to a tenancy node. Keys are hashed at rest, validated in
constant time on a cached hot path, and shown exactly once at creation. A ServiceAccount
authenticated by a valid key can act, authorized by its M3 role grants.

Because M3 was built kind-agnostic, the authorization surface barely moves: role grants, the
grant store, both caches, and grant-change invalidation all already accept any principal PRN.
The **new** work is the credential itself (hashing, token format, constant-time validation), the
service-account/api-key domain + persistence, the API-key bearer authenticator, the cached
introspection path, and the management wire surface.

**Acceptance criteria (from the issue):**

1. Keys issue and revoke; validation is **constant-time**; **revoked/expired keys are denied**.
2. A **service account can act, authorized by policy (M3)**.

Scope posture: **full scope in one PR** (all five issue bullets, including cached introspection
and property-based validation tests), matching the M1/M3 single-large-PR rhythm. §17 decomposes
it into ordered commits.

## 2. Decisions (settled during brainstorm; refined by the Stage 2 challenge — see §18)

| # | Decision | Choice |
|---|----------|--------|
| D1 | ServiceAccount authz modeling | **Reuse the unified `Pgs::Iam::Principal` type** (M3 D3). An SA is a `principal` PRN (`prn:pgs:iam:::principal/<uuidv7>`) with `kind = "service_account"`. The **only** authz-path change is un-hardcoding `kind = "user"` in the entity-slice loader (§8). No Cedar schema entity change, no engine change, no grant-store change, no cache change. Grants, `GrantRoleRequest.principal_prn`, and the `roles.rs` `resource_type == "principal"` gate all keep working unchanged. |
| D2 | Key hashing at rest | **HMAC-SHA-256 with a server-side pepper** (a config secret), not argon2 or bare SHA-256. API keys are 256-bit random tokens, not human passwords: a memory-hard KDF buys nothing against brute force and is far too slow for a per-request hot path; the pepper means a DB dump alone cannot validate keys. Deterministic → enables an indexed lookup. Verify is constant-time (D3). |
| D3 | Token format & validation | Shown-once token: `pgs_sk_<keyid_b64url>_<secret_b64url>`. `keyid` = the ApiKey's UUIDv7 (kernel-minted) — embedded so introspection is an **O(1) primary-key lookup**, never a scan. `secret` = 32 random bytes (256-bit). Stored: `key_hash = HMAC-SHA-256(pepper, secret)` (unique), a display `prefix`, and scope/status/expiry. **The plaintext token is never persisted.** Validate: length-cap → parse → b64url-decode `keyid` → PK lookup → `hmac::Mac::verify_slice(stored_hash)` (RustCrypto HMAC verify is inherently constant-time — no `subtle` dep) → assert `status = active` and `expires_at` unset-or-future. Malformed input → an `ApiKeyDefect` whose detail appears in `Debug` only (never `Display`/logs), mirroring `TokenDefect`. |
| D4 | Key authorization model | The key **authenticates as the SA**; authorization comes entirely from the SA's M3 role grants (AC "authorized by policy (M3)"). The key stores a scope PRN + optional action/role-scope metadata, but v1 does **not** enforce key-level downscoping — the metadata is persisted and returned for a later milestone (§15). |
| D5 | Introspection caching vs revocation | A Redis **positive-validation cache** reusing M3's shared `ConnectionManager`, keyed by `keyid`, short TTL. Revoke/expire **evicts** the key's entry so denial is immediate (satisfies "revoked/expired keys are denied", not merely "within TTL"). Expiry is also re-checked on every cache read. Cache miss/outage **fails open to Postgres** (a miss is a real DB validation, never an accept). Memory + Redis impls behind a port, selected by config (mirrors M2's `jwks_cache` / M3's authz cache). |
| D6 | `last_used_at` | **Throttled best-effort.** Updated at most once per `last_used_throttle_secs` (default 60) per key, off the request's critical path, errors swallowed. Coarse `last_used` is acceptable; write amplification on the hot path is not. |
| D7 | ApiKey identity & addressing | Plain **UUIDv7 PK** (kernel-minted), addressed by UUID in the management API (`/v1/service-accounts/{sa}/api-keys/{id}`), mirroring role-grants. The key has **no PRN of its own**; its `keyid` in the token is this UUID. Scope is a tenancy-node PRN. |
| D8 | Non-OIDC principal representation | Generalize the authenticated-principal type. `AuthnPrincipal` and the transport `AuthContext` carry a `Credential` enum — `Oidc { issuer, subject }` \| `ApiKey { key_id }` — replacing the flat OIDC `issuer`/`subject` fields. Downstream reads only `principal_id`, so blast radius is the two auth seams + the OIDC resolve path. |
| D9 | Management actions | Seven **new fine-grained Cedar actions** (matching the existing 27-action convention): `CreateServiceAccount`, `GetServiceAccount`, `ListServiceAccounts`, `ArchiveServiceAccount`, `IssueApiKey`, `RevokeApiKey`, `ListApiKeys` — added to `SCHEMA_SRC`, the `Action` enum (`as_wire`/`is_write`/`ALL`), and the `platform_admin` + `org_admin` system-role templates, authorized against the SA's owner node (or a `Root`-scoped admin). |
| D10 | SA ownership | An SA is **owned by exactly one tenancy node** (org/team/project) via `owner_*` columns + a `ck_service_account_owner` exactly-one-of discriminator (mirroring `role_grant` scope). Ownership is the SA's home for listing + management authorization; it is distinct from role grants (which give the SA its powers, possibly at other nodes). Name is unique per owner (`uq_service_account_owner_name`). |
| D11 | Wire surface | A **new `ServiceAccountService`** (proto): SA CRUD + `IssueApiKey`/`RevokeApiKey`/`ListApiKeys`. `IssueApiKeyResponse` carries the one-time plaintext token; `ListApiKeys` returns records **without** secrets (prefix + status + `last_used` + expiry). A key-introspection RPC/endpoint mirrors token introspect. **No new grant RPCs** — existing `GrantRole`/`RevokeRole` accept any `principal_prn`. |
| D12 | Configuration | New `[api_keys]` config block: `pepper` (**required** secret via env/figment), `key_prefix` (default `pgs_sk_`), `max_token_bytes`, `default_expiry_days` (optional), `last_used_throttle_secs`, and `introspect_cache { backend, redis_url, ttl_secs }`. Validated in `validate()`; documented in `iam.toml.example`. |
| D13 | ADR | **Opens the "API-key & secret handling" ADR** (per the issue), recording: HMAC-SHA-256+pepper over argon2/SHA-256, token structure + entropy, shown-once, constant-time verify, cache-evict-on-revoke, no plaintext at rest. Set Accepted at GATE 1. |
| D14 | Crypto deps & entropy | New workspace dep **`hmac`** (RustCrypto; `sha2`, `base64`, `rand`, `getrandom` already present). Entropy (32 random bytes, pepper handling) lives in the **service adapter** via `OsRng`, behind a `KeyMaterial`/`SecretHasher` port — the pure `paigasus-kernel`/`paigasus-iam-core` stay `getrandom`-free (preserves the `wasm-getrandom-free` gate). `deny.toml` license/advisory review for `hmac` (RustCrypto is broadly already vendored). |

## 3. Token model & validation (the crux of AC-1)

### 3.1 Anatomy

```
pgs_sk_<keyid_b64url>_<secret_b64url>
└──┬──┘ └────┬─────┘  └─────┬──────┘
 prefix    ApiKey UUIDv7   32 random bytes (256-bit), OsRng
```

- `prefix` (`api_keys.key_prefix`, default `pgs_sk_`) makes keys greppable in secret scanners and
  lets the credential router (§7) cheaply distinguish an API key from an OIDC JWT.
- `keyid_b64url` = base64url(no-pad) of the 16-byte UUIDv7 → the DB primary key. Not secret.
- `secret_b64url` = base64url(no-pad) of 32 CSPRNG bytes.

### 3.2 Persisted columns (never the plaintext)

`api_key { id (=keyid), service_account_id, scope node ref, prefix (display, e.g. pgs_sk_AbC3dEf…),
key_hash = HMAC_SHA256(pepper, secret) [unique], status, expires_at?, last_used_at?, created_at,
revoked_at?, scope_actions? (json), scope_roles? (json) }`.

### 3.3 Validation path (pure `verify` in the domain; I/O in the adapter)

1. Length-cap the presented string (`max_token_bytes`) — reject early (DoS guard, mirrors M2's
   `max_token_bytes`).
2. Strip `prefix`; split on `_` into `keyid` + `secret`; base64url-decode both. Any structural
   failure → `ApiKeyDefect::Malformed` (no secret material in the error).
3. b64url-decode `keyid` → `Uuid` → **primary-key lookup**. Missing row → reject (unknown key).
   `keyid` is caller-known, so short-circuiting here leaks nothing about the secret.
4. `Hmac::<Sha256>::new_from_slice(pepper).chain_update(secret).verify_slice(&row.key_hash)` —
   **constant-time** comparison of the full tag. Mismatch → `ApiKeyDefect::BadSecret`.
5. Assert `status = Active`; assert `expires_at` is null or `> clock.now()`. Else
   `ApiKeyDefect::Revoked` / `Expired`.
6. On success → resolve the SA `Principal` → an `AuthnPrincipal { principal_id, kind:
   ServiceAccount, status, credential: ApiKey { key_id } }`.

The pepper is the HMAC key (any length; `validate()` requires ≥32 bytes of decoded key material).

## 4. Domain model (`rs/crates/libs/paigasus-iam-core/src/`, pure — no serde/sqlx)

### 4.1 `principal.rs`
Add `PrincipalKind::ServiceAccount` (`as_str` → `"service_account"`, `parse`, round-trip test).
`principal.kind` has no CHECK constraint, so no migration ALTER is required.

### 4.2 New `service_account.rs`
```rust
pub struct ServiceAccount {
    pub principal_id: PrincipalId,   // 1:1 with a Principal (kind = ServiceAccount)
    pub owner: TenancyNodeRef,       // org | team | project (D10)
    pub name: String,                // validated via validate_name (reuse M1)
    pub status: PrincipalStatus,     // Active | (Disabled — see below)
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}
impl ServiceAccount { pub fn new(id, owner, name, now) -> Result<Self, DomainError> }
```
Follows the `User` template (references `Principal` by id). A disabled/archived SA denies auth.
Reuse `PrincipalStatus`; if a second status is needed, extend that enum (its `as_str`/`parse`
round-trip test comes along).

### 4.3 New `api_key.rs`
```rust
pub struct ApiKeyId(Uuid);                       // plain UUID (D7)
pub enum   ApiKeyStatus { Active, Revoked }      // as_str/parse + test
pub struct ApiKey {
    pub id: ApiKeyId,
    pub service_account_id: PrincipalId,
    pub scope: TenancyNodeRef,                   // node the key is scoped to (D4 metadata)
    pub prefix: String,                          // display only
    pub status: ApiKeyStatus,
    pub expires_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    pub last_used_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub revoked_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    pub scope_actions: Vec<Action>,              // stored, unenforced in v1 (D4)
    pub scope_roles: Vec<String>,                // stored, unenforced in v1 (D4)
}
pub enum ApiKeyDefect { Malformed, BadSecret, Revoked, Expired }  // detail in Debug only
```
Plus a pure `NewApiKey` value carrying the freshly minted plaintext (returned once) separate from
the persisted `ApiKey`. Pure `parse_token`/`format_token` helpers live here; the CSPRNG + HMAC
are behind ports (§4.5), so the domain stays deterministic and testable.

### 4.4 `authn.rs`
Introduce `Credential`:
```rust
pub enum Credential { Oidc { issuer: Issuer, subject: String }, ApiKey { key_id: ApiKeyId } }
```
`AuthnPrincipal` swaps its flat `issuer`/`subject` for `credential: Credential` (+ keeps
`principal_id`, `kind`, `status`, `expires_at`). `PrincipalContext` is unchanged.

### 4.5 `ports.rs`
- `IdGenerator`: add `new_service_account_id() -> PrincipalId`, `new_api_key_id() -> ApiKeyId`.
- New `SecretHasher` port: `hmac(&self, secret: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>` and
  `verify(&self, secret: &[u8], expected: &[u8]) -> bool` (constant-time) — pepper injected into
  the adapter, so the domain never sees raw pepper.
- New `KeyEntropy` port: `fn new_secret(&self) -> [u8; 32]` (adapter uses `OsRng`).
- New `ServiceAccountRepository` (`create` [principal+SA in one txn], `find`, `list_by_owner`,
  `set_status`) and `ApiKeyRepository` (`issue`, `find_by_id`, `revoke`, `list_by_service_account`,
  `touch_last_used`) — `#[async_trait]`, `: Send + Sync`, return `RepositoryError`, added to the
  object-safety assertion. New `ConflictKind` variants (`ServiceAccountNameTaken`,
  `ApiKeyHashCollision`).

### 4.6 `value.rs`
Add any needed `DomainError` variants (`InvalidServiceAccountName` reuses `InvalidName`; add
`InvalidApiKeyToken` for structural token errors surfaced at the domain boundary).

### 4.7 `lib.rs`
`pub mod service_account; pub mod api_key;` + extend the re-export block.

## 5. Persistence (`services/paigasus-iam`, migration `m0005_create_service_accounts_and_api_keys`)

### 5.1 Tables
- **`service_account`** — shared PK `principal_id UUID` FK→`principal(id)` `ON DELETE CASCADE`
  (mirrors `user`); `owner_org_id`/`owner_team_id`/`owner_project_id` nullable UUIDs +
  `ck_service_account_owner CHECK (num_nonnulls(owner_org_id, owner_team_id, owner_project_id) = 1)`;
  `name TEXT`, `status TEXT`, `created_at`/`updated_at`. `uq_service_account_owner_name` scoped per
  owner (composite unique across the three owner cols + name, NULL-aware via a partial index per
  owner kind). FKs to `organization`/`team`/`project` by string alias (per the m0002+ pattern).
- **`api_key`** — `id UUID` PK; `service_account_id UUID` FK→`service_account(principal_id)`
  `ON DELETE CASCADE`; `scope_org_id`/`scope_team_id`/`scope_project_id` + `ck_api_key_scope`
  disjunction; `prefix TEXT`, `key_hash TEXT` with `uq_api_key_hash UNIQUE`, `status TEXT`,
  `expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`, `last_used_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`, `created_at`, `revoked_at NULL`,
  `scope_actions TEXT NULL` (JSON), `scope_roles TEXT NULL` (JSON); `ix_api_key_service_account`
  on the FK. All uniques/checks via raw `ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT <name>` (names are
  load-bearing for `conflict_kind`). Enum columns are TEXT (no native PG enum).

Registered in `migration/mod.rs` (5th `Box::new`), `entities/mod.rs`, `persistence/mod.rs`
(`pub use` + `conflict_kind` branches for the two new constraint names).

### 5.2 Entities & adapters
- `entities/service_account.rs` (shared-PK `belongs_to` principal, mirrors `user.rs`),
  `entities/api_key.rs` (own UUID PK, empty `Relation`, adapters query directly).
- `pg_service_accounts.rs`, `pg_api_keys.rs` — `#[derive(Clone)]` over `DatabaseConnection`,
  `*_to_model`/`model_to_*` hand-mapping (a parse failure on stored data → `Backend`, never a
  silent default), pagination via `Page` + `ORDER BY created_at, id`.
- **Creation mirrors `create_user`:** `principal` row + `service_account` row in one transaction,
  principal first. Issuing a key is a single insert. `touch_last_used` is a throttled `UPDATE`
  (adapter-side guard: skip if `last_used_at > now - throttle`).

## 6. Application layer (`services/paigasus-iam/src/application/`)

- `service_accounts.rs`: `CreateServiceAccount`, `GetServiceAccount`, `ListServiceAccounts`,
  `ArchiveServiceAccount` — each `authorize.check(actor, Action::X, owner_node)` before acting;
  create mints via `IdGenerator` + `Clock`, then `repo.create`.
- `api_keys.rs`: `IssueApiKey` (authorize `IssueApiKey` on the SA's owner/scope → mint id + secret
  via ports → hash → persist → return `NewApiKey` with plaintext once), `RevokeApiKey` (authorize
  → set status Revoked + `revoked_at` → **evict cache**), `ListApiKeys` (authorize → paginated,
  no secrets).
- `authenticate_api_key.rs`: `AuthenticateApiKey` (mirrors `AuthenticateToken`): parse+validate
  (cache-first, §9) → `AuthnPrincipal` for the SA; `introspect_api_key` → `PrincipalContext`
  (principal + role grants) reusing M3's membership/grant paging.
- Register in `application/mod.rs`; wire in `AppState::new` (repos + `KernelIdGenerator` +
  `SystemClock` + the new hasher/entropy/cache adapters).

## 7. Authentication wiring (API-key bearer — the sibling authenticator)

The token→`AuthContext` seam is centralized in `adapters/auth.rs` + two enforcement call-sites
(`http/auth_middleware.rs::require_bearer`, `grpc/authn.rs::AuthEnforce::call`), both of which
call `state.authn.resolve(&token, Enabled)` today. Add **one credential-router branch** at each:
if `bearer_from_headers(...)` starts with `api_keys.key_prefix` → `state.api_key_auth.resolve(token)`,
else the existing OIDC `resolve`. Both yield an `AuthnPrincipal` → the **same** `AuthContext`
insertion, so nothing downstream (handlers, authz middleware) changes. The `WiredAuthenticator`
memory/redis enum is the precedent for building `api_key_auth` in `AppState::new`.

API-key auth errors funnel through the existing `AuthnApiError`/`authn_status` (401
`invalid_token`, 403 `principal_inactive`, 503 `unavailable`) — an `AuthnError` mapping for the new
`ApiKeyDefect`s (no secret material in any response).

## 8. Authorization (SA as a first-class principal)

- **Entity-slice loader** (`pg_entity_slice.rs`): the one hardcode to change — `principal_entity()`
  reads `kind` from the `principal` row (already fetched by PK) instead of the literal `"user"`.
  With SAs minted as `principal` PRNs, `to_cedar_uid` yields `Pgs::Iam::Principal` and the slice
  is correct with no schema change.
- **New management actions** (D9) added to `authz/schema.rs` `SCHEMA_SRC` (`appliesTo { principal:
  [Principal], resource: [Root, Organization, Team, Project] }`), `authz/action.rs` (`Action`
  enum + `ALL`/`as_wire`/`is_write`), and the `platform_admin`/`org_admin` templates in
  `authz/roles.rs`. Adding actions to the schema re-runs write-time validation of every system
  template (existing test).
- **Cache invalidation for SA grant changes is already automatic**: `role_grant.principal_id` is
  kind-agnostic and `PgRoleGrantStore::grant/revoke` already bump `policy_gen`. No new mechanism.
- **Runtime authorization of an acting SA** flows through the unchanged `CedarAuthorizer` path:
  authenticated SA principal + its role grants → `is_authorized`.

## 9. Introspection & caching (`adapters/api_keys/` or `adapters/authz/`-style)

- Port `ApiKeyValidationCache { get(keyid) -> Option<CachedValidation>; put(keyid, &v, ttl);
  evict(keyid) }`. `CachedValidation` = `{ principal_id, sa_status, expires_at }` (enough to rebuild
  `AuthnPrincipal` and re-check expiry on read; **never** stores the secret or the hash).
- `MemoryApiKeyCache` + `RedisApiKeyCache` (reusing M3's shared `ConnectionManager`), key
  `iam:apikey:<keyid>`, TTL `introspect_cache.ttl_secs`. **Fail-open**: `get` errors → `None`
  (fall through to DB); `put` errors → logged+swallowed. `RevokeApiKey` and any read that observes
  expiry call `evict(keyid)`. Backend chosen by config (memory/redis enum), matching M2/M3.
- Hot path: `AuthenticateApiKey.resolve` → parse token → `cache.get(keyid)` hit (re-check expiry) →
  else DB validate (§3.3) → `cache.put`. Introspection endpoint uses the same path.

### 10.1 Proto (`contracts/proto/paigasus/iam/v1/iam.proto`)
New `ServiceAccount` and `ApiKey` messages (string `prn`/ids, `google.protobuf.Timestamp`,
embedded `AuditMetadata`, UPPER_SNAKE status enums, `_UNSPECIFIED = 0`). New `ServiceAccountService`:
`CreateServiceAccount`, `GetServiceAccount`, `ListServiceAccounts` (uint32 limit/uint64 offset),
`ArchiveServiceAccount`, `IssueApiKey` (→ `IssueApiKeyResponse { ApiKey api_key; string token; }` —

token `Introspect`). Buf codegen via the committed prost/tonic pipeline (`moon run contracts:generate`);
breaking-change gate respected (reserve-and-add).

### 10.2 HTTP (axum)

  token; management errors via `ApiError`/`TenancyError`).
- Introspection (unauthenticated, body-limited, merged outside the bearer layer like token

- New DTOs in `http/dto.rs` (`ServiceAccountDto`, `ApiKeyDto` [no secret], `IssueApiKeyResponseDto`

`convert.rs` gains `to_proto_service_account`/`to_proto_api_key`/`to_introspect_api_key_response`.

## 11. Configuration (`config.rs`, figment) — new `[api_keys]` block

```toml

key_prefix              = "pgs_sk_"
max_token_bytes         = 512
```

`validate()`: pepper present + length; non-zero TTL; redis_url iff redis; sane `max_token_bytes`.

Opens the **API-key & secret handling ADR** (Notion), recording D2/D3/D5/D13: HMAC-SHA-256+pepper
